title: The Children of Edward (The Princes in the Tower)
source: Musée du Louvre, Paris (public domain); photographed on loan at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon, 2014. Wikimedia Commons: Les Enfants d'Édouard - Paul Delaroche - MBA Lyon 2014.jpg (4008 x 3196 px)
caption: Two boys. A locked room. The dog hears someone. #truecrime #princesinthetower #delaroche #oilpainting #unsolvedmysteries
_verify: VERIFIED, Wikipedia EN (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Children_of_Edward): Delaroche 1830, oil on canvas 181 x 215 cm, Louvre; the Princes in the Tower, Edward V and Richard of Shrewsbury, imprisoned after Edward IV's death; Richard III usually believed to have ordered their murder, no concrete evidence; 'the small dog in alert' and light entering under the door 'suggest an imminent entrance'; book shows a miniature of the Annunciation; ribbon of the Order of the Garter on one child's leg; shown at the Salon of 1831, called a 'tearjerker'; bought by the State 1831.

VERIFIED, Patrick Comerford blog (Wallace Collection version): 'an ominous shadow can be seen at the bottom of the door'; 'the dog and perhaps the young Duke of York sense the arrival of the approaching murderers'; Edward the 12-year-old uncrowned boy king; open missal with the Annunciation.

GENERAL HISTORY (low risk, not re-sourced today): Edward IV died April 1483; Edward V born Nov 1470 (12); the boys were not seen after summer 1483; their uncle Richard of Gloucester crowned Richard III July 1483; bones of two children found in the Tower in 1674. Slides avoid Richard's exact age (sources say 9 or 10).

slides.headline: Two boys. A locked room. The dog hears someone.
slides.sub: Paul Delaroche, The Children of Edward, 1830

slides.headline: London, 1483
slides.text: 1483, the Tower of London. King Edward IV has just died. His older son, only twelve, should now be crowned King Edward V.

slides.headline: The brothers
slides.text: Instead, he and his little brother Richard are kept in the Tower by their uncle. Now they sit on a bed, holding on to each other.

slides.headline: A prayer book
slides.text: They were reading a prayer book, open on a painting of the Annunciation. Then something made them stop.

slides.headline: A king's ribbon
slides.text: On one leg, the ribbon of the Order of the Garter. A boy king, with nothing left but a ribbon.

slides.headline: The dog
slides.text: But look at the little dog. It has turned away from the boys, alert, staring at the door.

slides.headline: Under the door
slides.text: Because under the door, there is light, and a shadow. Someone is standing on the other side, about to come in.

slides.headline: They know
slides.text: Look at their eyes. The younger one has heard it too. Their uncle has already taken the crown as Richard III.

slides.headline: Vanished
slides.text: The princes were never seen again. In 1674, workers found the bones of two children in the Tower. Who opened that door?
